name: Baseline
description: Endogenous fast-transition baseline: model defaults with 2025-level carbon prices and no further policy. NOT aligned with IEA STEPS, though after the 2026 demand-side corrections (efficiency-corrected electricity accounting, IEA sector shares, historical intensity decline, retail pricing) it is far closer than before: 2050 electricity demand ~38k TWh (~0.7x STEPS ~55k, formerly 4x), fossil electricity share ~16% in 2050 falling to ~0 by 2075 (vs ~35% in 2050 STEPS), warming ~2.3C by 2100 (vs ~2.4C STEPS-consistent). The transition is still faster than STEPS because Way-et-al learning rates keep solar+storage undercutting fossil dispatch. GDP growth is near-flat (~0.1%/yr to 2100): with realistic demand accounting, useful energy per worker stagnates and the Ayres-Warr channel no longer produces an energy-abundance boom. Treat as the model's own no-policy trajectory, not a replication of any IEA scenario.
